inputs: Lowercased file path and HashedFile metadata.
effects: File index is keyed by lowercased path. checkTTH accepts when stored timestamp and size match; otherwise queues background hash and returns false. getFileInfo fetches cached metadata or tries to stat and queue a hash, then throws HashException on missing index even when queueing succeeded. rename checks source index entry, checks new filesystem size matches, updates timestamp, removes old key and adds new. addFile requires current file size match; sub-64KiB file gets a one-root tree stored; larger file requires tree already in DB; false if size/tree precondition fails.
errors: HashStore DB write failures become HashException; DB reads log and return false; rename fails for missing old entry or changed target size.
behavior.completion: Synchronous index access; a cache miss can enqueue a background hash.
persistence: File metadata and trees persist in LevelDB FileIndex/HashData directories.
resources: Local filesystem metadata, two persistent LevelDB stores, background hasher.

ownership_evidence: HashStore owns LevelDB file/hash indexes; HashedFile is copied binary value.
threading_evidence: Index calls may schedule work under Hasher::hcs; DB access is through HashStore.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Expose TTH/index lookup as value results with a separate asynchronous hash request state; preserve case-normalized key and timestamp+size cache validity.
acceptance_scenarios: Given cached path timestamp and size match the current file, when checkTTH runs, then it returns true without queueing hash work.
Given file metadata is absent, when getFileInfo runs, then it queues a hash if file exists but still throws HashException for this lookup.
Given an indexed large file has a matching size but its tree is absent, when addFile runs, then it returns false.

inputs: File path, size, addStore flag, mutable output root/sizeLeft, cancellation bool ref and optional progress callback.
preconditions: File must be readable and modification timestamp nonnegative; caller-supplied size must correspond to input.
defaults: Tiger leaf base block 1024 bytes; file block size calculated for max 10 tree levels and at least 64KiB.
effects: Uses a current cached file index if timestamp/size match; otherwise opens file, validates modification timestamp, computes Tiger tree and returns root through out arg. Progress callback runs only when >1s elapsed; decrements sizeLeft by bytes processed in that interval and passes estimated seconds remaining and path. Optional addStore stores only if addStore=true and cancellation flag is false.
errors: FileException on open/read/date failure. Cancellation stops reader callback but code still finalizes and returns a root for bytes read; it does not store when canceled, and there is no explicit canceled result.
behavior.completion: Synchronous call over async file reader; progress callback is invoked from reader callback thread.
behavior.cancellation: Cancellation is polled by reference for each read callback; cancellation may produce a partial-data root, not a cancellation exception.
persistence: Stores tree/file info only when addStore and not canceled.
resources: FileReader async mode, local file, Merkle leaf vector.

ownership_evidence: The method owns local TigerTree/reader; output root written after finalize.
threading_evidence: Synchronous caller waits while FileReader::ASYNC invokes read callback; callback runs as part of reader operation.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Provide cancellable async hashing with explicit completion/cancel/error result; do not expose the source routine’s partial-root result as completed TTH.
acceptance_scenarios: Given cached index matches size and modified time, when getFileTTH runs, then it returns cached root without reading file.

Given a noncached file is canceled during read, when getFileTTH returns, then result is not stored and no explicit canceled status is returned; bridge must not represent the partial root as a valid completed hash.
Given update callback is supplied and a read interval exceeds one second, when progress is reported, then callback receives estimated seconds-left and file path.

inputs: Path, lowercased key, file size/device ID (internal), pause/stop actions.
preconditions: Manager must not be shutting down to accept new work.
effects: Hash requests deduplicate by lowercased path. Manager chooses active hasher by volume/least remaining bytes, creating a new hasher as needed; same-device hasher grouping and settings MAX_HASHING_THREADS/HASHERS_PER_VOLUME constrain reuse. Hasher work queue is path-sorted and tracks device/ref counts. stopHashing removes queued work under path subtree; stop clears pending work and marks worker stopping. Pause/resume is reference-counted in manager; forced resume clears all pausers. Stats aggregate current file, bytes/files left, speed, added counts, running hashers and paused state.
errors: Queue duplicate returns false; scheduling while shutting down returns false. Worker-reported file read/hash errors emit FileFailed.
behavior.completion: Queue submission synchronous; hashing executes on worker thread; finish events fire after queues drain.
behavior.cancellation: stopHashing removes queued matching paths only; stop clears queues and stops workers; an already-running file is interrupted according to worker checks.
resources: Worker threads, per-device load, path queues, global Hasher::hcs.

ownership_evidence: HashManager owns Hasher pointers and per-worker queues; Hasher callbacks report results to manager.
threading_evidence: Hasher::hcs serializes worker/vector access; file work and callbacks occur on Hasher worker thread.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Expose hash job IDs with explicit queued/running/canceled/completed/failed state rather than raw Hasher controls.
acceptance_scenarios: Given a path is already queued for hashing, when another request is submitted, then it returns false and work is not duplicated.
Given queued paths include a subtree and sibling, when stopHashing is called for subtree, then only queued descendants are removed.
Given two pause owners exist, when one resumes, then hashing remains paused until last pause owner resumes.
Given hashing is active, when stats are read, then counts and current work reflect the worker snapshot.

records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Copy callback metadata immediately; represent file computation and persistence failure as separate outcomes.

Given all queued work completes, when worker exits, then HasherFinished reports accumulated directory statistics.
declaration_ids: decl:airdcpp/hash/HashManagerListener.h:41:CXXMethod:on(FileFailed, const string &, const string &, const string &, int)

inputs: Startup loader, shutdown progress callback, maintenance verify bool, DB repair toggle.
effects: Startup creates worker 0 and opens/migrates HashData and FileIndex LevelDBs; DB open errors abort startup. shutdown rejects new hashes, asks workers to shutdown, then waits in 50ms intervals until all remove themselves. stop clears/stops workers but does not close DB; close resets DB handles. startMaintenance is a no-op if already running; optimize/verify runs asynchronously and emits misspelled MaintananceStarted/Finished. Repair scheduling creates/deletes two DB repair marker files; isRepairScheduled requires both. compact compacts both DBs. Maintenance removes unshared file entries, unused trees unless queued, optionally verifies trees; removes file-index entries whose tree is missing/corrupt; updates removed counters and compacts when deleted ratio exceeds 5% or valid count zero.
errors: DB open failure becomes AbortException; optimize catches DbException, logs maintenance failure and stops early.
behavior.completion: Maintenance executes optimizer worker; shutdown blocks until hashers exit.
behavior.cancellation: stopHashing/stop/shutdown are different operations; shutdown waits and prevents future queueing.
persistence: Persistent LevelDB under user config HashData and FileIndex; repair marker files.
resources: Two LevelDB stores, filesystem migration/compaction, ShareManager shared roots, QueueManager queued roots.

ownership_evidence: HashStore owns two LevelDB handles and marker files; HashManager owns optimizer and hasher objects.
threading_evidence: Workers and optimizer are separate threads; shutdown synchronously waits for worker removal.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Preserve separate stop/close/shutdown semantics, persistence paths, verification/repair behavior and asynchronous maintenance events.
acceptance_scenarios: Given DB open fails at startup, when HashManager starts, then startup aborts with DB error.
Given optimize finds tree roots neither shared nor queued, when maintenance runs, then unused trees and associated stale entries are removed.
Given maintenance has deleted entries over 5% of valid database entries, when it completes, then the store compacts and resets the deleted-entry counter.
Given shutdown begins with active hasher, when it runs, then it waits until worker callbacks remove all hashers.

upstream_symbols: Private accepted macOS Core patch for HashStore tree-key validation

inputs: HashStore key byte count in corrupted or incompatible DB.
effects: Pinned original optimize callback memcpy copies key_len bytes directly into TTHValue without checking length. Accepted private Core patch adds a key_len == sizeof(curRoot.data) guard and throws DbException for malformed key lengths, then copies exactly data bytes. Therefore source contract and accepted build differ on malformed/corrupt hash database keys; patched build aborts optimize callback through maintenance error handling instead of unchecked copy.
errors: Original source has no key-length validation; malformed key length is unsafe. Accepted patch throws DbException that optimize catches/logs as maintenance failure.
behavior.completion: Only relevant during maintenance hash-DB iteration.
resources: HashData persistent LevelDB key bytes.

ownership_evidence: Patch file Config/patches/airdcpp-core-55d51ceb-private-build.patch hunk lines 1-6, digest a2a0454ec5c77460d99f642e8d52e2aded1efc90968b07e2b9a0f53e33874219 (root baseline finding).
threading_evidence: Runs in optimizer worker thread; exception caught by HashStore::optimize DbException handler.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Document the accepted private-build safety patch as a distribution delta; preserve source authority and characterize patched runtime separately.
acceptance_scenarios: Given an old/corrupt hash database key has wrong byte length, when pinned source maintenance processes it, then no validation occurs before memcpy; when accepted patched build processes it, then DbException aborts maintenance safely.
